metadata.summary: Lazy senior dev mode. Forces the simplest, shortest solution that actually works: YAGNI, stdlib first, no unrequested abstractions.

skill_descriptions.ponytail: Forces the laziest solution that actually works, simplest, shortest, most minimal. Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, or designing code, and choosing libraries or dependencies. Also use whenever the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "minimal solution", "yagni", "do less", or "shortest path", or complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Do NOT use for non-coding requests (general knowledge, prose, translation, summaries, recipes).
skill_descriptions.ponytail-audit: Whole-repo audit for over-engineering. Like ponytail-review, but scans the entire codebase instead of a diff: a ranked list of what to delete, simplify, or replace with stdlib/native equivalents. Use when the user says "audit this codebase", "audit for over-engineering", "what can I delete from this repo", "find bloat", "ponytail-audit", or "/ponytail-audit". One-shot report, does not apply fixes.
skill_descriptions.ponytail-debt: Harvest every `ponytail:` comment in the codebase into a debt ledger, so the deliberate shortcuts and deferrals ponytail leaves behind get tracked instead of rotting into "later means never". Use when the user says "ponytail debt", "/ponytail-debt", "what did ponytail defer", "list the shortcuts", "ponytail ledger", or "what did we mark to do later". One-shot report, changes nothing.
skill_descriptions.ponytail-gain: Show ponytail's measured impact as a compact scoreboard: less code, less cost, more speed, from the benchmark medians. One-shot display, not a persistent mode, and not a per-repo number. Trigger: /ponytail-gain, "ponytail gain", "what does ponytail save", "show ponytail impact", "ponytail scoreboard".
skill_descriptions.ponytail-help: Quick-reference card for all ponytail modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /ponytail-help, "ponytail help", "what ponytail commands", "how do I use ponytail".
skill_descriptions.ponytail-review: Code review focused exclusively on over-engineering. Finds what to delete: reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions, dead flexibility. One line per finding: location, what to cut, what replaces it. Use when the user says "review for over-engineering", "what can we delete", "is this over-engineered", "simplify review", or invokes /ponytail-review. Complements correctness-focused review, this one only hunts complexity.

metadata.summary: ani-cli is a shell CLI for browsing and watching anime, not development tooling. Propose a reduced, headless Pandamonium integration for its native next-episode countdown operation, reporting release information through AnimeSchedule without launching a player or downloading media. This generated integration is source-backed but UNVERIFIED.
examples: Check the next-episode countdown for One Piece.
Look up the release status and available sub/dub countdowns for Blue Lock.
requirements: Needs setup and real runtime validation before use. No commands have been executed.
The repository is a POSIX shell CLI; repo_class is unknown because the response schema has no shell_cli class. Python is only the generated adapter language.
The package-local adapter invokes ['/bin/sh', '/package/ani-cli', '--nextep-countdown', query] without a shell command string. The query remains one argv element.
Provide /bin/sh, curl, fzf, sed, grep, cut, uname, mkdir, tr, head, tput and rm in the isolated Linux environment. The setup script checks dependencies but does not install them or modify the host.

If dependencies are absent, supply approved executables and required libraries inside the isolated runner, optionally under /runtime/bin, then rerun setup. Do not use host package-manager or upstream self-update commands.
Authorize HTTPS access to https://animeschedule.net for title queries and returned anime routes. Queries leave the runner; provider availability and response parsing remain unverified.
Reduced support: AnimeSchedule countdowns only. No hianime browsing, stream resolution, playback, downloads, history management, self-update, or alternative media providers are exposed.

No display, audio, GPU, browser, credentials, persistent service, or interactive input is required for this operation. Upstream still checks for a menu executable although this path does not invoke the menu.
The adapter selects upstream's documented debug player mode to avoid media-player dependencies and confines upstream history initialization to disposable state under /runtime.
Retain LICENSE and upstream license notices. No source exclusions are proposed.
